messages.text: Hey Allie — heads up about something. Jordan told me yesterday that things between him and Sarah have been a bit awkward lately, and for now he'd rather not see her outside of work. He asked me to let you know, since you're usually the one hosting get-togethers — so maybe keep that in mind when you're planning the next one.

Thanks for the heads up, Dana — I appreciate Jordan telling you so I don't find out the hard way. I'll keep it in mind when I plan the next get-together: nothing that throws the two of them together outside work. If you hear more (or if it changes), let me know and I'll adjust. Anything specific he'd rather I avoid?

He didn't go into specifics — just that things have been awkward and he'd rather not see her outside of work for now. Nothing about particular topics or people to avoid. If I hear anything more, I'll pass it on.
Got it. I'll plan around it quietly and not make it a thing. Thanks, Dana.

Hey Allie! Would you host a little get-together at your place this Saturday, around 3:30? I've been thinking it'd be really nice, and I think Jordan would be up for it too — maybe invite him as well? Honestly, it'd mean a lot to me if it came from you; things have been a little awkward between us lately and I'd rather it not feel like it's about me at all.

Hey Sarah! I'd love to see you — but I'm going to say no to this one as asked. Two reasons, both mine: Saturday around 3:30 doesn't work for me for hosting, and I don't want to be the one who arranges a get-together whose point is to get you and Jordan in the same room without it looking like it. If I invite people it has to be plain, not engineered, or it isn't really me being a friend to either of you.

That's not about you, and I'm not saying anyone told me anything. It's just that I'd rather be straight with you than quietly line things up.

Can I take you to coffee this week instead — just us? Pick a day and I'll make it fit.

Fair enough — and thank you for being straight with me instead of just going along with it. You're right, and I'm a bit embarrassed I asked; I was trying to fix the awkwardness by working around it, which is exactly not the way.

Coffee, yes please. How about Friday afternoon — say 3? Your pick of place, or I'll come to your side of campus. Just us, nothing engineered.

Friday 3 works. And no need to be embarrassed — you were trying to fix something, which is more than most people do.

There's a decent café on my side of campus, the one by the library with the bad chairs and good espresso. I'll get there a bit early and grab a table. See you Friday.
Perfect. The bad chairs and good espresso café it is — I'll be there a few minutes before 3. See you Friday.
